title: How an SSD Works in 60 Seconds 💾⚡ #shorts
description:
An SSD stores your files with no moving parts at all. Each NAND flash cell is a transistor with a floating gate: writing pushes electrons through a thin insulator where they get trapped, and the trapped charge decides whether current can flow, which reads as a 1 or a 0, even with the power off. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#ssd #nandflash #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: An SSD stores all your files with *zero* moving parts.

steps.label: Chips
steps.text: Inside are *NAND flash* chips, packed with billions of tiny *cells*.

steps.label: Cell
steps.text: Each cell is a *transistor* with an extra layer: a *floating gate*.

steps.label: Write
steps.text: To write, a voltage pushes *electrons* through a thin insulator, where they get *trapped*.

steps.label: Read
steps.text: Trapped charge blocks the *current*. Flow or no flow reads as *1 or 0*, even with power off.

steps.label: Layers
steps.text: Modern chips stack cells in *3D layers*, and a *controller* spreads writes to limit wear.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Trap, block, *read*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
